svg.title: Who may call whom, and what enforces each allowed path
svg.text: Rows call, columns are called. Green: allowed, with the port or rule that admits it. Grey: refused. Amber: not restricted in this build.
Between services: an ingress network policy on the
called service, naming the caller and the port.
Into the sandbox: only the router, on 8080 and 9090.
Out of the sandbox: only the gateway, on 3128.
To the Kubernetes API: a small RBAC role.
What the grey cells rely on
Every called service has an ingress policy, so a
caller that is not named is refused.
Pods with no service-account token cannot use the
Kubernetes API, though nothing blocks the connection.
A sandbox has no route to anything else.
Only the gateway pods and the sandboxes have an
egress network policy. Other platform pods are
limited by what they are written to call, and by
the absence of credentials, not by a network rule.
Adding egress policies is a hardening step.
